subject: FinWise — Load test coordination & SLO confirmation
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: John Miller <john.miller@finwise.com>, SaaS Ops <ops@finwise.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: FinWise — Load test coordination & SLO confirmation

Hi John / team,

Great to meet earlier — quick recap and next steps so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled: 

Summary of SLOs you mentioned on the call:
- P95 latency target: <= 250ms (end-to-end, token generation)
- Sustained throughput target: 100 requests/sec
- Peak concurrency: 50 concurrent streams/sessions
- Streaming behavior: needs partial token streaming to the client (chunked responses)

What Redwood needs from FinWise to run the test:
1) Confirm a 2-hour test window (preferred Tue 2027-03-15 10:00–12:00 PT) or propose an alternate window.
2) Provide test account(s) or API key with test-only access we can use (no production data).
3) IP allowlist: we’ll provide IPs to allowlist on your firewall; please confirm when done.
4) Preferred load tool: you mentioned k6 for the scenario — please attach your test script if you’ve already authored one.

Action (owner):
- Logan: attach our reference k6 script + test account creds (attached).
- FinWise: confirm window + create test keys + allowlist IPs.
- Marissa/Rishi: be on call for escalation and spectral monitoring during the run.

Attachments:
- finwise-k6-script-v1.js (application/javascript) [attached]
- test-account-creds.txt (text/plain) [attached]

Let me know if the SLO summary above matches what you expect and if the proposed window works. Once confirmed, we’ll send the IPs and the runbook (observability links, what metrics we’ll capture).

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123

--

Subject: Re: FinWise — Load test coordination & SLO confirmation

Thanks, Logan — the recap looks right. Confirming a few items from our side:

- Window: Tue 2027-03-15 10:00–12:00 PT works for us.
- Test accounts: ops will create a scoped API key (test-only) and share credentials with your team.
- IP allowlist: ops needs the list of source IPs you’ll use; once we have them we’ll request firewall exceptions.
- Scripts: we have a Locust-based scenario that simulates our UI + streaming clients; attaching a short README with what the script does. If k6 is easier for you, we can export a simplified k6 scenario as well.

Streaming: we need to validate that partial responses are chunked every ~100ms on average — that’s the client expectation. Let us know if Redwood needs any custom headers or connection keepalives during the run.

I’ll get the test key and ops contact over to you by EOD.

John
Director, Platform Engineering
FinWise

- Window: 2027-03-15 10:00–12:00 PT

- They have a Locust scenario but are ok with k6; we attached our k6 script (finwise-k6-script-v1.js) to the thread.

I’ll follow up to schedule a quick sync with infra if you want to walk the runbook.

Thanks,
Logan

Notes for the run:

- Observability: we will share a Grafana link during the run and capture token latency, p50/p95/p99, error rates, and CPU/GPU utilization.
